record.description:
Use searchable Linux directory modes and descriptor-relative restoration. Isolate potentially blocking physical identity and SQLite pre-handle opens behind finitely owned platform cancellation mechanisms. Classify cancellation from direct operation evidence, and resolve repository fixtures from deterministic assembly metadata rather than mapped caller paths.
Converted from FR-MCP-USECASE-016 on 2026-10-19 (operator: "If it is in a FR, then that FR needs to be converted to a TR"; answers "Merge into its TR (Recommended)" and "FR-001, delete FRs (Recommended)"). FR-MCP-USECASE-016 stated: Use-case persistence and its supporting contained rollback, physical workspace identity, SQLite opening, cancellation classification, and repository evidence paths shall remain safe and finitely completing on every supported platform, including deterministic CI builds, while preserving exact provider failures and truthful supersession evidence.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-USECASE-001; TEST: TEST-MCP-USECASE-019

acceptanceCriteria.text: Linux rollback directories retain owner search and execute permission, nested restoration reproduces file contents and mode, and all mutations remain contained.
Physical workspace identity resolution completes within a finite bound on Windows and non-Windows without caller-thread blocking, cancellation gaps, abandoned workers, or silent platform returns.
SQLite connection opening is finitely bounded before native-handle publication on every supported platform and leaves no worker, handle, callback, interrupt, pool, or lifecycle leak.
Only outcomes precisely attributable to requested cancellation become OperationCanceledException; independent I/O, disposal, and provider failures retain their original type and details.
Repository and Agent Help fixtures discover their root from true external deterministic builds with mapped CallerFilePath and no MCP_REPOSITORY_ROOT override.

Every supported platform executes an applicable native contract assertion: a platform-specific test is a Category=Integration test tagged Platform=Linux or Platform=Windows for the host it applies to, which TR-MCP-NUKE-019 AC-1 and AC-2 route to that host's MigrationIntegrationTests and require to run and pass there, and it passes only as TR-MCP-USECASE-019 AC-008 states (operator 2026-10-30: "D3: dedupe lane rules (Recommended)"); no unit test depends on the platform or on the process environment, directly, through a test helper or through the production code it calls: a test whose outcome can change with the value of an environment variable it reads or writes, directly, through a test helper or through the production code it calls (for example a temporary-folder lookup that takes its folder from a variable and creates it), a test that imports the process environment into configuration (AddEnvironmentVariables or a default host builder), and a test that asserts on an environment value a child process inherits are Category=Integration tests that set and restore every variable their assertions or the code they call depend on, every name of a fallback chain the code reads, both forms where a variable has a canonical (QBrainAi, QBRAINAI_) and a legacy (Mcp, MCP_) form, and the tests that write the process environment run one at a time (operator 2026-10-21: "Fix both, strengthen ACs", "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option" and "Approve, strengthen AC-006/008 (Recommended)"; operator 2026-10-26: "Strengthen AC, move 14 (Recommended)", "Dependence + proof AC (Recommended)" and "Fix source, strengthen AC (Recommended)"; hostile validation findings R5-F2, R6-F1 and R7-F1). The hostile-environment runs are out of scope: they are not part of this criterion or its evidence (operator 2026-10-27: "Get ride of the hostile runs enforcing integration test separation.  I have already stated this once." and "Which I sated last night were out of scope."). An integration case may read the lane's own inputs without setting them: MCP_REPOSITORY_ROOT, the MCP_TEST_ connection variables the lane provisions, and, for an import that scans agent folders, the user's real profile folder, read only and never asserted on; every other variable its assertions or the code it calls depend on it sets and restores. A unit test asserts no wall-clock bound (operator 2026-10-29: "Environment ACs (Recommended)"; holistic review findings MCPT-11, SVC-6 and MCPT-12). These rules are stated here once for TR-MCP-USECASE-019 AC-008 as well; the environment-delta rule moved to FR-MCP-047 ac-1 (operator 2026-10-29: "Move criteria that are misplaced.  Unit tests are for FR, Integration tests are for TR."). A unit test that checks a recorded time (an auth rotation, a selection or a session transition) takes the clock values from test-owned scripted inputs and asserts them exactly; it never compares with the current time, never sleeps to separate two times, and its result cannot change with elapsed time, scheduling delay or a change to the system clock (hostile validation round 10 finding R10-F3; strengthened between rounds under the operator's "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option" and "don't gate on me between rounds", 2026-11-03). This covers every recorded time a unit test checks, including the creation and update times a service stamps on a record it stores: the test supplies the service's clock as scripted times and asserts that each stamp equals the scripted time the service read (sibling sweep before round 11 of hostile validation round 10 finding R10-F3, 2026-11-03, under the same rulings). A wall-clock bound is an assertion whose outcome depends on how much real time passes: an elapsed time compared with a limit, or work the test expects to have happened during a short real-time wait (for example a periodic tick, a file-system event or a debounce); such a test is an integration test. A timeout whose only effect is to fail a test that would otherwise hang, set far above the time the awaited step needs, is not a wall-clock bound (holistic read before round 11, 2026-11-03, under the same rulings). A cancellation or timeout that a unit test arms on a real timer is such a wait when a step the test asserts must happen before the timer fires (finding of the hostile validation round 11 that stopped without a verdict, 2026-11-03, under the same rulings). Of the two sentences above, the hang-guard sentence governs: a timer a unit test arms whose only effect when it fires is to fail a test that would otherwise hang is a hang guard, not a wall-clock wait, even when an asserted step must finish before it fires. A test-armed cancellation or timeout is a wall-clock wait when its firing changes what the code under test does (for example it cancels or times out the operation whose outcome the test asserts) and an asserted step must happen before it fires. "Far above" means at least 100 times the longest real or scripted delay of the awaited step; a step with no real or scripted delay meets it for any positive timeout (holistic read before hostile validation round 12, finding B4; operator 2026-11-03: "Strengthen + margin (Recommended)"). The longest real or scripted delay of the awaited step is the sum of every real or scripted delay on its path: the waits, polls and delays the test scripts and the production waits, polls and deadlines the step passes through, read from the sources, never a measured run time (third holistic read before hostile validation round 12, finding d3; operator 2026-11-04: "Fix it", read as the recommended option "Strengthen + headroom"). A wait that happens only under a condition the step can meet, such as the 150 ms sleep before Microsoft.Data.Sqlite retries a statement that found the database busy, counts in that sum once for each poll on the path (fourth holistic read before hostile validation round 12, finding g1; operator 2026-11-04: "Strengthen: include them").

The rejected fourteenth receipt is preserved with an explicit supersession notice, and the fifteenth evidence records every failed, inconclusive, and passing run with independently verified hashes and command mappings.

record.title: Cross-platform bounded native I/O and deterministic evidence

record.description: Preserve Windows behavior. Linux uses bounded shell-free systemctl/tar operations, installed-unit preflight, platform RID/apphost selection, shared preservation paths,0700 backup directories/0600 archives, ownership/mode/ACL/xattr preservation, failure restoration and same health checks. No SQL database export or automatic binary rollback claim.

acceptanceCriteria.text: UpdateService selects Windows or Linux at runtime; Windows defaults/launcher remain compatible; Linux x64/arm64 use extensionless apphost; unsupported hosts fail before changes.

Both platforms preserve live appsettings.yaml and configured DataFolder with legacy fallback. Linux also preserves unit/drop-ins/environment files and Unix ownership/modes/ACLs/xattrs through a private retained archive.

Linux validates installed service identity and stage before stop; backup precedes replacement; restore precedes start; service executable and server/workspace health must pass. Failures preserve recovery artifacts and never report success.

Mocks-first tests and full applicable unit suites pass with zero failures/skips; independent gates pass; existing local Linux service update preserves configuration/data and trusted workspace behavior.

Every Build.Tests ServiceUpdateTests case runs and passes on Linux and on Windows with no skip. A case whose Linux check needs a Linux-only facility (a FIFO, Unix file modes, GNU tar ACL and xattr preservation, unlinking a directory symbolic link with File.Delete) asserts on Windows the outcome the helper produces there for the same input (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 C2, triage-report-cdf116ad, as BUG-BASELINE-004 did for Windows-only tests; StatDouble_ReportsRegisteredSpecialFileAsFifo, and the Windows cases of LinuxPreflight_RejectsSpecialStageFiles, LinuxPreflight_RejectsSpecialApphostAndTextInputs, LinuxArchive_UsesPrivateMetadataPreservingCommands, LinuxReplacement_DoesNotFollowSymlinks and LinuxPreflight_RejectsSymlinkRootAndNonexecutableStage).

The Linux update reads a unit whose systemctl show output repeats a property on separate lines (systemd 262 prints one EnvironmentFiles line per environment file) and validates and preserves every environment file those lines name. Redeploy of 2026-11-04: on systemd 262 the update stopped at the second EnvironmentFiles line before any service change. Added under the operator's standing word of 2026-10-26: "if you surface new AC, add them without waiting for approval".
